opening.text: Before anyone builds a house, they pour a foundation. It isn't pretty. Most of it ends up underground. But everything else rests on it. Conversion works like that. It begins with a small, quiet start. Then, over years, the whole life is built on it.

mainMessage.text: Conversion is not one moment. It is a foundation we keep building on, with God's help.

blocks.text: **Pour the foundation** A testimony is where it starts. It begins with a small desire to believe.

But behold, if ye will awake and arouse your faculties, even to an experiment upon my words, and exercise a particle of faith, yea, even if ye can no more than desire to believe, let this desire work in you, even until ye believe in a manner that ye can give place for a portion of my words.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Converted unto the Lord” from the October 2012 general conference.
Testimony is the beginning of and a prerequisite to continuing conversion.
Start with what you can believe today.
**Build the walls** Walls go up one board at a time. Conversion shows in what we do again and again.

And as sure as the Lord liveth, so sure as many as believed, or as many as were brought to the knowledge of the truth, through the preaching of Ammon and his brethren, according to the spirit of revelation and of prophecy, and the power of God working miracles in them—yea, I say unto you, as the Lord liveth, as many of the Lamanites as believed in their preaching, and were converted unto the Lord, never did fall away.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Converted unto the Lord” from the October 2012 general conference.
Consistently being true to the gospel is the essence of conversion.
Steady habits hold a house up.
**Build to the plan** A builder follows the plans. A converted person learns to follow God's will.

Nevertheless they did fast and pray oft, and did wax stronger and stronger in their humility, and firmer and firmer in the faith of Christ, unto the filling their souls with joy and consolation, yea, even to the purifying and the sanctification of their hearts, which sanctification cometh because of their yielding their hearts unto God.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Conversion to the Will of God” from the April 2022 general conference.
True conversion is brought about by the conscious acceptance and commitment to follow the will of God.
Conversion is a choice to follow His plan.
**Work with the Master Builder** We can't do this alone. The Holy Ghost helps us know what is true. And it takes time.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost. And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
Mark L. Pace, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Conversion Is Our Goal” from the April 2022 general conference.
Long-lasting conversion is a lifelong process.
Give the work time.
**A new heart for the house** Something changes inside the house, not just outside. The people of King Benjamin said the Lord changed their hearts.

And they all cried with one voice, saying: Yea, we believe all the words which thou hast spoken unto us; and also, we know of their surety and truth, because of the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent, which has wrought a mighty change in us, or in our hearts, that we have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Burying Our Weapons of Rebellion” from the October 2024 general conference.
Burying our weapons of rebellion leads to a unique joy.
A changed heart is a happy one.
**Open the doors** A finished house is meant to have guests. A converted person wants to help others find the same shelter.
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Conversion to the Will of God” from the April 2022 general conference.
Our personal conversion includes the responsibility to share the gospel of Jesus Christ with the world.
Conversion makes us want to share.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their faith grew deeper. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma remembers Jesus Christ

blocks.text: Alma had turned away from God. In his worst hour, he remembered what his father had taught him about the Savior. He called out.

Now, as my mind caught hold upon this thought, I cried within my heart: O Jesus, thou Son of God, have mercy on me, who am in the gall of bitterness, and am encircled about by the everlasting chains of death. And now, behold, when I thought this, I could remember my pains no more; yea, I was harrowed up by the memory of my sins no more. And oh, what joy, and what marvelous light I did behold; yea, my soul was filled with joy as exceeding as was my pain!
His change began with one cry to Jesus Christ. It lasted the rest of his life.

mainMessage.text: Conversion is the slow, steady work of the Spirit in our hearts. Small choices add up to a changed life.

But behold, if ye will awake and arouse your faculties, even to an experiment upon my words, and exercise a particle of faith, yea, even if ye can no more than desire to believe, let this desire work in you, even until ye believe in a manner that ye can give place for a portion of my words.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Converted unto the Lord” from the October 2012 general conference.
Testimony is the beginning of and a prerequisite to continuing conversion.
A trickle is enough to begin.

Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Converted unto the Lord” from the October 2012 general conference.
Consistently being true to the gospel is the essence of conversion.
Consistency carves the canyon.

Nevertheless they did fast and pray oft, and did wax stronger and stronger in their humility, and firmer and firmer in the faith of Christ, unto the filling their souls with joy and consolation, yea, even to the purifying and the sanctification of their hearts, which sanctification cometh because of their yielding their hearts unto God.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Conversion to the Will of God” from the April 2022 general conference.
True conversion is brought about by the conscious acceptance and commitment to follow the will of God.
Yielding to God is how we flow with Him.
**Water over time** No one hurries a river. The Holy Ghost teaches us what is true, and it takes many seasons.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost. And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
Mark L. Pace, Sunday School General President, said this in his talk “Conversion Is Our Goal” from the April 2022 general conference.

Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Burying Our Weapons of Rebellion” from the October 2024 general conference.
Burying our weapons of rebellion leads to a unique joy.
A changed heart brings a new joy.
**Water for others** A river feeds the land downstream. A converted person strengthens those who are near.
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Conversion to the Will of God” from the April 2022 general conference.
Our personal conversion includes the responsibility to share the gospel of Jesus Christ with the world.
What we receive, we pass on.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a hard moment changed them for good. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Saul receives his sight

blocks.text: Saul had fought the Church. Then he met the Lord on the road to Damascus. A disciple named Ananias was sent to help him.

And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
Saul became Paul, and he gave his life to the work. A great change came, and it was carried on over many years.

story.title: The king bows down

blocks.text: A Lamanite king wanted what Aaron taught. He was willing to give up everything to have it.

And it came to pass that when Aaron had said these words, the king did bow down before the Lord, upon his knees; yea, even he did prostrate himself upon the earth, and cried mightily, saying: O God, Aaron hath told me that there is a God; and if there is a God, and if thou art God, wilt thou make thyself known unto me, and I will give away all my sins to know thee, and that I may be raised from the dead, and be saved at the last day. And now when the king had said these words, he was struck as if he were dead.
He asked God to show him. God answered. He gave up what held him back in order to know God.

story.title: Thomas says, My Lord and my God

blocks.text: Thomas had doubts. When the Savior stood in front of him, his doubts settled.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they made a lasting promise to God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The people bury their weapons

blocks.text: A whole people were converted. They decided they would never fight again. They made a covenant with God.

And now it came to pass that when the king had made an end of these sayings, and all the people were assembled together, they took their swords, and all the weapons which were used for the shedding of man’s blood, and they did bury them up deep in the earth. And this they did, it being in their view a testimony to God, and also to men, that they never would use weapons again for the shedding of man’s blood; and this they did, vouching and covenanting with God, that rather than shed the blood of their brethren they would give up their own lives; and rather than take away from a brother they would give unto him; and rather than spend their days in idleness they would labor abundantly with their hands.
Their change was complete, and they kept their promise. The path they walked was clear for all to see.

application.text: First, think of one promise you have made to God. Second, ask how well you are keeping it. Third, take one step this week to keep it better.
